---
title: "Campi Flegrei glass geochemistry"
---

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ELSTE-Master/Data-Science/main/Data/Smith_glass_post_NYT_data_majors.csv"
data = pd.read_csv(url)
data = data[data["Eruption"].isin(["Monte Nuovo", "Astroni 6", "Fondi di Baia"])]
data = data.dropna(subset=["SIO2", "K2O"])
n_analyses = len(data)
n_eruptions = data["Eruption"].nunique()
mean_sio2 = round(float(data["SIO2"].mean()), 2)
```

We use the glass-composition dataset (@Smith2011), selecting the Monte Nuovo, Astroni 6 and Fondi di Baia eruptions. We retain analyses with both SiO~2~ and K~2~O measurements. Oxides are used as supplied, without anhydrous normalization; counts refer to analyses, not necessarily independent samples.

The selection contains **`{python} n_analyses` glass analyses** from **`{python} n_eruptions` eruptions**, with a mean SiO~2~ content of **`{python} mean_sio2` wt. %**.

@fig-geochemistry shows the retained analyses; @tbl-geochemistry summarizes their compositions.

```{python}
#| label: fig-geochemistry
#| fig-cap: "Glass compositions for the selected Campi Flegrei eruptions."
#| fig-alt: "Scatter plot of potassium oxide against silica, colored by eruption."
plt.figure(figsize=(6.6, 2.7))
sns.scatterplot(data=data, x="SIO2", y="K2O", hue="Eruption")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-geochemistry
#| tbl-cap: "Mean oxide contents by eruption (wt. %)."
#| output: asis
table = data.groupby("Eruption")[["SIO2", "K2O"]].mean().round(2)
print(table.to_markdown())
```
